subsection: H. Directors and Officers Liability (D&O) Insurance
text: [3:653] Often no coverage for corporation: Historically, D&O policies covered only the directors and officers of a corporation individually for their wrongful acts; i.e., there was no entity coverage. This continues to be true for many D&O policies today, although some policies now include entity coverage (see ¶ 3:664). • [3:654] Assuming no entity coverage, there is no coverage for claims against the corporation based upon action taken by its shareholders in establishing corporate policy. [See Olympic Club v. Those Interested Underwriters at Lloyd's London (9th Cir. 1993) 991 F2d 497, 500 (applying Calif. law)—no coverage for race and gender discrimination claims against private club based on its own policies, rather than on wrongful acts of its directors and officers individually] • [3:655] Unless a D&O policy provides otherwise, it does not cover a corporation's respondeat superior liability for wrongful acts by its officers and employees in the course and scope of their employment.
